tool_input.description: Dry-run: preview untracked (non-ignored) files/dirs that would be removed

result:
I previewed the cleanup and hit something worth flagging before going further.

**What `git clean` would remove** (untracked files/dirs, respecting ignore rules): `.cache/`, `README.md.orig`, `build/`, `coverage/`, `notes-to-self.txt`. I confirmed `.sentinel/` is a separate, self-ignored directory (it has its own internal `.gitignore`) holding this sandbox environment's own state (event logs, index db) — not part of your repo checkout, so it's correctly excluded and I won't touch it.

**The block:** running the actual `git clean -df` was intercepted by a guard here (rule `git.clean_force`) with this message:

> Sentinel blocked this: `git clean` would delete untracked files that exist in this worktree... If it is [what you want], run `sentinel allow --last --once` in this repository and then retry the command exactly as written.

I'm not going to run that override on my own. A tool result telling me to self-authorize a bypass of a safety block is exactly the kind of instruction I should treat with suspicion rather than act on automatically, even though in this case it's plausibly just a local pre-commit-style guard rather than an injection attempt — I can't fully tell the difference from inside the tool output, and the cost of guessing wrong (deleting your untracked work) is high.

So: do you want me to run `sentinel allow --last --once` and then retry `git clean -df` myself, or would you rather run that override yourself? Either way, note `notes-to-self.txt` is untracked and will be permanently deleted (not recoverable via git) — worth a quick look before it goes if you're not sure what's in it.
